record.context_brief: Chaos on singular loci of integrable systems
record.original_question: For an integrable Hamiltonian system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold, determine how complicated the dynamics can be on singular submanifolds where the n commuting first integrals lose functional independence, including whether chaotic behavior can occur on such tiny singular sets.

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Consider an integrable system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold, which has n first integrals in involution, functionally independent almost everywhere. How wild could such a system be on a singular submanifold, where the integrals become dependent? What are constraints dictated by the integrability? Could one observe a chaos on some tiny submanifold of an integrable system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $H:M\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth Hamiltonian. Assume the Hamiltonian system defined by $H$ is Liouville integrable: there exist $n$ smooth functions $f_1=H,f_2,\dots,f_n:M\to\mathbb{R}$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ for all $i,j$, and are functionally independent (i.e., $df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\neq 0$) on an open dense subset of $M$. Let 
$$\Sigma\;=\;\{\,x\in M\;:\;df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_n\,(x)=0\,\}$$
denote the singular set on which the integrals fail to be functionally independent. The Hamiltonian flow of $H$ preserves $\Sigma$ and each connected component of its strata.

Investigate the dynamical complexity of the Hamiltonian flow restricted to $\Sigma$:

(a) Describe what constraints Liouville integrability imposes on the dynamics on $\Sigma$ (and on its individual smooth strata).

(b) Determine whether the restricted dynamics on $\Sigma$ can exhibit chaotic behavior — for instance, positive topological entropy, a horseshoe, or a hyperbolic invariant set with a dense orbit — even when $\Sigma$ is a "tiny" (low-dimensional, measure-zero) submanifold of $M$.

(c) If chaos is possible, exhibit an explicit smooth ($C^\infty$ or real-analytic) example of a Liouville integrable system on a compact symplectic manifold whose restriction to the singular locus $\Sigma$ has positive topological entropy; if it is impossible, prove the corresponding rigidity theorem.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how complicated (and in particular how chaotic) the dynamics of a Liouville integrable Hamiltonian system can be on its singular locus appears to be an open research problem. Bolsinov–Taimanov constructed real-analytic integrable geodesic flows whose singular set carries positive topological entropy, showing chaotic-type behavior on singular subsets is possible in specific examples, but a general description of the constraints that integrability imposes on the dynamics restricted to the singular submanifold, and a complete answer to whether arbitrary chaotic behavior may appear on arbitrarily small singular submanifolds, has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Integrable geodesic flows on Riemannian manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Bolsinov and Taimanov (1999) constructed an example of an integrable geodesic flow with positive topological entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Chaos-like behavior (positive topological entropy) can coexist with Liouville integrability, supported on singular invariant subsets; but a general theory is not available.

status_evidence.title: Geometry and Dynamics of Integrable Systems (Bolsinov, Morales-Ruiz, Zung)
status_evidence.snippet: Lecture notes describing singularities of integrable systems via their relation to bi-Hamiltonian systems and obstructions to integrability.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of singularities of integrable systems is an active area of research, with no complete classification of admissible restricted dynamics.
